ops.title: A daemonkit state-root wipe is not durable until the artifact store and staged binaries are current too
ops.body:
Found 2026-08-29, ten minutes after declaring the fleet's state-root wipe complete — a dead root reappeared on its own. Upgrading every Homebrew package is **necessary but not sufficient** to finish a daemonkit state-root migration.

## What happened

After the v0.23.0 migration, `ls ~/com.*` matched nothing and the plant-a-decoy negative check had passed. Ten minutes later `~/com.yasyf.cc-review/` was back, holding **only `locks/start.lock`** — no `daemon.sock`, no `daemon.records` — created at 19:30:56 while the live daemon (pid 67314, status 0) was serving happily from `~/.daemonkit/a/com.yasyf.cc-review/`.

A directory containing a lock and nothing else is the fingerprint: something *started* under the old root's path calculation without ever becoming the daemon.

## The cause: two independent copies of a consumer, and Homebrew touches neither

`~/.daemonkit/bin/` holds two differently-named kinds of executable, and it is easy to conflate them:

- **Label-named** (`com.yasyf.cc-review`, `com.yasyf.cc-orchestrate`, …) — daemonkit's *staged, sealed* daemon binary. The LaunchAgent's `ProgramArguments` points here, never at the Homebrew path. Re-staged by daemonkit's ensure path.
- **Bare-named** (`cc-review`, `cc-present`, `cco`, `binrun`) — the **artifact store**: a version-exact executable resolved from a declarative descriptor, each with a `<name>.meta.json` recording `policy`, `build`, `digest`, `size` and `mtime`.

The culprit was the bare-named one. `~/.daemonkit/bin/cc-review` was **v0.33.3, dated Jul 27**, with `{"schema":2,"policy":"build","build":"v0.33.3",…}` — a locally-built artifact compiled against a pre-v0.22.0 daemonkit, so its path calculation still yields `~/<label>/`. `brew upgrade` moved `/opt/homebrew/bin/cc-review` to 0.35.0 and left this copy untouched. Anything resolving cc-review through the artifact store therefore ran a binary that had never heard of the new root.

Three others sat in the same state: `cc-present` 0.31.3, `cco` 0.15.3 (both Jul 27), and the staged `com.yasyf.codex-ask` at 1.10.0 (Aug 16).

**Note the plugin descriptors were innocent** — `~/.claude/plugins/cache/cc-review/cc-review/0.35.0/bin/cc-review.binrun` correctly pins `"static": "0.35.0"`. The stale copy was the store's own build-lane entry, not a stale pin.

## The remedy, and what it revealed

Moving the four bare-named artifacts and their `.meta.json` siblings to `~/.Trash/` (never `rm` — they are outside any repo) resolved it. `cc-review list` and `cco --version` both worked immediately afterward and reported current versions, and no old root has reappeared since.

The interesting part is what came back. `cc-review`, `cc-present` and `cco` did **not** regenerate — they are `policy: build` entries, rebuilt on demand from local checkouts that are now current. `binrun` **did** regenerate, byte-identical at **0.1.1 with its original Jul 23 mtime**, because its descriptor pins that version and the store faithfully re-materialised it, restoring the recorded mtime from the meta. That is the artifact store working exactly as designed — version-exact resolution from a declarative descriptor — and it is the distinction that matters operationally:

- a **build-lane** entry going stale is drift, and clearing it fixes it;
- a **pinned** entry is not stale at all, and clearing it changes nothing.

binrun is harmless here regardless: it imports only `daemonkit/artifact` and `ghrelease`, and resolves the home directory through `internal/realhome` rather than `paths.Agent`, so it never computes an agent root.

## The checklist this adds to a state-root migration

Upgrading packages and wiping dead directories is step one. Before declaring a host clean, also:

1. **Audit `~/.daemonkit/bin/`**, both naming conventions. `for f in ~/.daemonkit/bin/*; do "$f" --version; done` against each one's expected version. A file older than the migration is a live hazard.
2. **Clear stale build-lane artifacts**, and expect pinned ones to return unchanged — check `policy` in the `.meta.json` before concluding anything from a reappearance.
3. **Re-check the old roots after a delay**, not immediately. The reappearance here took ten minutes and was triggered by ordinary tool use, not by anything the migration did. An immediate check reports success either way.
4. A directory holding **only `locks/start.lock`** means an old-era binary ran, not that a daemon relocated. Diagnose the binary, not the daemon.

## Related

daemonkit re-stages a label-named binary as part of the ensure path, so a stale *staging* is normally overwritten before its LaunchAgent is bootstrapped — observed directly when `cco fleet status` re-staged cc-orchestrate 0.16.0 → 0.17.0 and registered the agent in one step. That protection does **not** extend to the artifact store, which is why the bare-named copies are the ones that bite.

See also [[a-daemonkit-consumer-migrates-when-it-ships-not-when-its-main-is-bumped]] — same theme one layer up: what is installed decides the state layout, not what any repository's `main` says.
